finding.summary: C246's source-level characterization is supported at the pinned CSSC commit. A syntactically valid REFINE_ARGUMENT payload can name step/alignment IDs absent from the live branch, pass proposal validation after controller finalization, and then be returned as an exact no-op by the structural reducer when none of those IDs hits live state.
details: StructuredActionProposal.validate() routes REFINE_ARGUMENT payload validation through _argument_payload_errors(). That function checks only each AlignmentSpec via _alignment_errors(); it does not compare payload step IDs/alignment IDs to live branch state, require payload step/alignment coverage, or compare payload IDs to SearchAction.target_step_ids.
SearchAction.validate() explicitly states that target_step_ids are not cross-checked against an actual ArgumentGraph; live cross-validation is delegated to the structured executor.

The controller's _finalize_kind() reconstructs a new SearchAction with kind, target_branch_id, allowed_mutations and rationale but does not pass target_step_ids, so the dataclass default () replaces any proposal pins. This verifies the target-step erasure premise at the exact pinned commit.

apply_argument() for REFINE_ARGUMENT computes whether any refined step ID hits existing branch.argument.steps or any refined alignment ID hits existing branch.alignment. If neither hits, it returns the exact input workspace without successor/version advance.
finding.scope_guard: This is a static primary-code reachability verification at commit f40a3d3a. It does not by itself demonstrate frequency in live model-generated runs, end-to-end exploit impact, or the proposed C247-C253 journal design. C247-C253 are design proposals/future contracts, not verified current implementation behavior.

do_not_infer: Do not count C247-C253 as implemented crash-safe journal features.
Do not infer that every REFINE proposal no-ops; only the no-live-hit path does.
Do not infer live incidence or downstream proof-quality effect from static reachability alone.
